aiRule: Attempt problems yourself first. Use AI only as reviewer/mentor after your attempt.
goal: Google SWE interview readiness (L3/early L4) while becoming a stronger independent engineer.

skillTargets.target: 160+ curated problems with pattern recognition; mediums under ~35 minutes
Production-quality idioms for backend coding rounds and take-home clarity
Explain OS, DBMS, and OOP trade-offs without slides in under 8 minutes
Trace a request path and justify timeout, retry, and auth choices
Complete one HLD and one LLD mock per month with explicit trade-offs
Think-aloud coding, STAR-L behavioral stories, and Googleyness examples

phases.title: Foundations
phases.focus: DSA patterns, Go language basics, CS fundamentals refresh, daily think-aloud habit
outcomes: Solve array/hash and two-pointer mediums without pattern hints
Write idiomatic Go with table tests for small utilities
Explain process vs thread and ACID in plain language
Complete first weekly retention assessment

phases.title: Core Skills
phases.focus: Trees, graphs, Go concurrency and HTTP, networking depth, first system design methods
outcomes: BFS/DFS and topo sort under time pressure
Build a handler chain with context cancellation in Go
Diagram DNS to TLS handshake for a browser request
Draft URL shortener HLD with back-of-envelope numbers

phases.title: Interview Depth
phases.focus: DP and advanced graphs, DB transactions, distributed design topics, mock interviews
outcomes: Recognize DP state transitions on common Google variants
Implement SQL transactions and explain isolation anomalies
Design rate limiter and notification system with failure modes
Two Pramp or interviewing.io sessions with written retro

phases.title: Integration
phases.focus: Mixed timed sets, LLD drills, behavioral bank, weak-area sprints
outcomes: Weekly Saturday mock covering coding + one design prompt
Ship a small Go service with tests, middleware, and structured logs
Five polished STAR-L stories mapped to Googleyness attributes
Revisit bottom-quartile DSA tags until green

phases.title: Polish
phases.focus: Full-loop simulations, resume narrative, rest and confidence calibration
outcomes: Two full-day onsite simulations (coding, design, behavioral)
One-page system design cheat sheet from memory
Question list for interviewers and thank-you templates ready
Light review only—no new heavy topics in final 72 hours before real loops

weeklyRhythm.weekday: Sunday–Friday ≈120 min study: DSA practice (60–70) + skill learn (Go/fundamentals/networking/design) (35–40) + communication speak (15). No timed assessments on study days.
weeklyRhythm.weekend: Saturday only ≈240 min: weekly mock + assessment (LeetCode/Pramp/interviewing.io). No regular study backlog scheduled on Saturday.
weeklyRhythm.assessment: All tests, assessments, and mocks are Saturday-only. Sunday–Friday are study days. You may complete any future day's tasks ahead.
